added: New Prism setups use the permanent name Minecraft - Progression Survival.
Iron Tools has separate goals for 16 pumpkin pies and one smithing table.
changed: Gold tool practice now requires 224 mined blocks, 224 soil blocks and 128 logs. Other Gold requirements stay the same.
Iron Tools asks you to capture cod, salmon, pufferfish and tropical fish in buckets instead of catching another batch with a rod.
Copper Tools combines catching and cooking 16 cod into one task.
Working redstone circuits no longer need a fixed dust count or a straight wire layout.
Personal Settings uses the Journal checkbox style, keeps highlights clear of helper text and scrolls below its fixed title and close button.
Existing progress, unlocks and paid rewards are preserved.
removed: Journal task descriptions and the historical-completion suffix.
The gear tooltip while Personal Settings is open.
Outdated text claiming shields need five Iron-tier skeleton kills. Shields can be crafted and used as soon as Iron Armor is unlocked.

1.0.0-rc.1.comparison: The first published release: the starting point for this history.
added: A personal Progression Journal, separate Armor and Tools tracks, and 53 optional XP quests.
Mining provenance, dungeon challenges, inventory-safe armor returns, and personal task and tier notifications.
A launcher-importable client pack and a reusable Windows server bundle, with pinned mod downloads.

1.0.0-rc.6.comparison: Compared with RC 1, the previous published release.
added: Journal 0.7.5 replaces 0.7.2.
Ore goals track fresh mining within each Tools tier instead of reusing lifetime totals.
changed: Combat counters follow the active Armor tier.
Mob difficulty focuses on health and damage scaling.
removed: Disabled Improved Mobs’ extra equipment, block breaking, stealing, flying mounts and other special behaviors.

1.0.0-rc.7.comparison: Compared with RC 6, the previous published release.
added: Journal 0.8.0, personal tier-completion supply bundles and enchanted Netherite capstones.
Optional Village Bounties and shield training, bringing optional quests to 55.
A fuller update guide that tells players to keep their old Prism instance and copy their settings.
changed: Swords and weapon crafting follow Tools progression. Armor focuses on matching personally crafted sets, combat and dungeons.
Weapon-specific kill goals begin at Copper; one eligible kill can fill a weapon goal and a mob goal.
Food and ore goals are spread across tiers, with once-only task XP and safe deferred rewards when inventories are full.
removed: Disabled enchanted-gear bounty rewards in this release; later versions introduce a new personal reward system.

1.0.0-rc.10.comparison: Compared with RC 7, the previous published release. Includes changes developed in the unpublished RC 8 and RC 9 builds.
added: Journal 0.9.0, collapsible quest categories and smarter reopening of the active tier.
Personal Village Bounties: seven offers, Gold-tier Elite access, fixed reward previews, owner-earned armor and safe deferred claims.
Five optional raider and raid-victory quests, bringing optional quests to 60.
changed: Shield crafting and use unlock together after five eligible Iron skeleton kills.
Armor tier supply rewards include 32 arrows from Leather through Diamond.
New bounty boards have waxed display signs, and the ten-bounty quest is called Village Bounties.
removed: Removed a private KubeJS settings file from the downloads. The game content otherwise matches the unpublished RC 9 build.

1.0.0-rc.14.comparison: Compared with RC 10, the previous published release. Includes the verified release-audit and tool fixes developed in RC 12 and RC 13.
added: Bows become usable at Stone Tools, when the journal asks you to craft one.
Quest categories remember each player’s choices across reconnects and game restarts, and show completed / total quest counts.
Protection for bounty boards and their three associated display signs in survival.
changed: Mining, chopping, digging, tilling and ore tasks require the exact current Tools tier and the correct tool type.
The original wooden bounty board and bottom-left tracker return, with scrollable rewards and a notification for each completed bounty.
New Hard and Elite bounty offers have 25% and 35% gear odds, with a 10% enchantment chance after gear is awarded. Previously rolled rewards stay the same.
Journal 0.9.9 retains the accepted journal and bounty improvements, with development-only behavior removed. Crossbow and shield gates are unchanged.
removed: Removed the Gold-tier diamond and redstone mining goals because a golden pickaxe cannot harvest them. Gold quartz stays.
Removed development audit commands, a test-only server shutdown hook, a test-mob credit exception and example scripts from the release.

1.0.0-rc.15.comparison: Compared with RC 14, the previous published release.
added: Iron Tools: build and activate a simple redstone circuit with your own switch, dust and piston or iron door.
Gold Tools: place 128 rails of any type and ride across 64 different personally laid rails in one continuous trip; visit a Nether fortress.
Diamond Tools: brew three useful potion types, craft twelve Eyes of Ender, find a stronghold and enter the End.
Optional quests for six useful potion types, ten distinct table-enchanted gear pieces and post-Dragon End-city/Elytra flight.
changed: The personal Ender Dragon advancement is the final Tools capstone. Earlier genuine Dragon/discovery proof counts; no second Dragon fight or duplicate Dragon payout is required.
Journal 0.9.11 verifies real construction, cart travel, table enchanting and personally initiated brewing. Insert brewing ingredients yourself and keep the stand open until the batch finishes.
Previously completed tiers and access stay completed. New work applies to active/future tiers, with historical-tier exemptions shown without inventing counters or replaying rewards.

1.0.0-rc.16.comparison: Compared with RC 15, the previous published release.
changed: Mature wheat, carrots and potatoes credit the player who harvests them, including crops planted by another player and existing village farms. Required and optional harvest goals use the same rule.
Planting stays personal. Immature crops, item pickups, cancelled breaks and duplicate callbacks do not earn mature-harvest credit.
Existing progress, completed tiers, earned access and reward receipts are preserved. Uses the existing Journal 0.9.11.
removed: Removed the requirement to harvest only crops you planted yourself. Sapling planting and growth goals stay personal.

1.0.0-rc.19.comparison: Compared with RC 16, the previous published release.
added: Public announcements for newly earned journal goals and equipment-tier advances, including player and tier context.
A 47-job bounty catalog: 10 Easy, 10 Medium, 15 Hard and 12 Elite, with destination-specific gathering, fish capture, treasure recovery, hunts and dungeon clears.
Separate clearing goals for all five dungeon types and the all-types challenge, requiring at least 90% of original spawners after a complete structure census.
Small Nether Dungeons in newly generated Nether terrain; explored terrain and existing worlds are preserved.
changed: Bows are available from Wood Tools; shields unlock at Iron Armor access. Crossbows retain their Iron Armor requirement.

Food preparation uses different vanilla dishes: Iron 16 pumpkin pies / 32 cookies; Gold 12 cakes / 12 suspicious stews; Diamond 12 rabbit stews / 16 golden carrots; Netherite 8 golden apples. Earlier bread, mushroom stew and cod work remain.
Cod cooking, brewing and bounty copper smelting credit ingredient contributors on completion, regardless of who collects output or whether the menu remains open.

Enemy scaling caps at difficulty 250 are 3x health, 2x melee damage and 1.5x projectile/explosion damage. Known old saved-enemy modifiers convert once, preserving damage taken and unrelated attributes.
Easy / Medium bounties pay 20-35 / 60-100 XP with guaranteed emeralds and supplies. Hard / Elite pay 180-260 / 400-600 XP with guaranteed unlocked-tier armor, emeralds and supplies.
Arrow supply rewards are 8 / 16 / 32 / 64 by difficulty. Exact rewards remain visible before acceptance; accepted contracts and pending payouts retain their original terms.
Combat and food wording is clearer, fallback journal rows are corrected, and existing progression, inventories and reward receipts remain preserved.
removed: The extra five-skeleton requirement for shield access.
Torch supply rewards and the overlapping generic Netherite feast requirement.
Output collection as the trigger for cod cooking credit.
